tool_input.command: for p in 'One LMS at two addresses' 'LMS OWNS THE PLAYER NAME' 'UUID ASK RESIDUALS' 'AN OFFER LOST IN FLIGHT' 'TWO NAMES IN FLIGHT LOOP' 'TWO LMS ON ONE HOST' 'A STOP CANNOT CUT THE NAME WRITE'; do echo "=== $p"; grep -rn "$p" docs/ledger/ | grep -v index.md | cut -c1-120; done
tool_input.description: Locate ledger entries for name-related phrases

result:
I found no high or medium findings. There is one low-severity hardening finding. Everything else I looked at is either correct or already settled in the ledger.

## Findings

**1. Low (hardening): `process_setd` assumes the incoming name ends with a NUL byte inside the packet** — `engine/slimproto.c:737`, `:742`, `:744`

- **The cause:** `slimproto_run` passes `process()` its static 4 KB receive buffer (`:828`, `:859`). Nothing ends the packet with a NUL, and leftover bytes from earlier, longer packets stay in the buffer. `strncpy` at `:737` stops after 64 bytes, but `LOG_INFO("set name: %s", setd->data)` (`:742`) and the confirmation `sendSETDName(setd->data)` (`:744`, which calls `strlen`) read until they find a NUL.
- **What goes wrong:** if a `setd` name ever arrives without its NUL, the player name picks up stale bytes, up to 63 of them.
  - That name is cut to whole characters, written to the `-N` file with `F_FULLFSYNC`, and the server is added to the server list.
  - The confirmation sends the longer, corrupted text back to LMS. LMS sees a value different from its own and takes it as a rename. Both sides then keep the corrupted name.
  - If the packet fills all 4096 bytes, `strlen` can run past the end of the array.
- **Why it's low:** upstream squeezelite has the same code. As far as I know, LMS 9.1 always ends the name with a NUL. I did not check this against the LMS source in this session. Before LyrionPlay, a bad name stayed in memory; now it is written to disk and sent back to LMS.
- **Fix:** take the name from at most `len - 5` bytes (`memchr` for the NUL, or copy into a terminated local buffer). Then use that copy for the log, the confirmation and `player_name`.

## Checked and not raised
- **UUID lookup using UDP port 3483 whatever the slimproto port** (`:1270`): declined, `TWO LMS ON ONE HOST`.
- **The ~500 ms wait before the HELO, and replies accepted only from the address asked** (`ask_server_uuid`, `:645–672`): declined, `UUID ASK RESIDUALS`.
- **A server with no UUID reply judged by its address**, including the rename loop when a held rename meets a second address. The suite pins this on purpose (`test_held_rename_two_addresses_no_uuid`). It is the settled residual under `One LMS at two addresses`.
- **The server list updated when an offer is fully sent, even if LMS never reads it** (`name_offered`, `:699`): accepted, `AN OFFER LOST IN FLIGHT`.
- **No server list at all means the empty answer goes to every server** (`:502`): by design, `LMS OWNS THE PLAYER NAME`.
- **The `.tmp` + `F_FULLFSYNC` + rename writes**: `A STOP CANNOT CUT THE NAME WRITE` and CODE-REVIEW 2026-10-15 (5)/(6).
- **Code I traced and found correct:**
  - `add_name_server`: the line matching, the `memmove` edge cases (last line, list full) and dropping the oldest line.
  - `fit_name` at 2-, 3- and 4-byte characters at the cut.
  - The buffer sizes in `file_holds`, `load_name_servers` and `store_name_servers`.
  - The 6-byte `"eUUID"` request: its trailing NUL is the tag's length byte.
  - The bounds checks in `parse_server_uuid`.
  - The confirmation sending LMS's full name, not the cut one, so a name over 63 bytes doesn't trigger a rename.

Two related cases I looked at and left out because I couldn't show they happen or do harm:
- **An empty name from LMS** (`setd` carrying only a NUL) would write an empty `-N` file, and the next start would offer the `-n` name. That only matters if LMS can hold an empty player name, and replacing an empty name with `-n` does little harm.
- **A name with a newline in it** is stored as sent, but only the first line is read back at the next start (`:1142`).

CLAUDE.md says a finding cleared during a review should be logged in the ledger in the same session. You told me not to modify any files, so I didn't add anything, and finding 1 isn't in the ledger yet. Everything in the "Checked" list is already logged.
